subject: Prompt sample inventory + sensitive-edgecase capture (post-demo follow-up)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Tran <olivia.tran@searchgrid.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Prompt sample inventory + sensitive-edgecase capture (post-demo follow-up)

Hi Olivia — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps for the eval phase so we can size the right config and pick model families: 

Summary from call:
- Primary use case: document search assistant (short answers + provenance links) for internal knowledge base.
- Typical query mix: 60% short factual questions, 25% multi-hop/contextual (2–4 docs), 15% instruction-style synthesis (summaries).
- Latency target: 200–350ms p95 on user-facing calls.
- Concern areas: (1) PII in examples (customer emails), (2) model hallucination on edge legal language, (3) cost per 1M tokens.

What we need from your side to move to a focused eval: 
1) Prompt samples: export ~200 representative user prompts across the three buckets above. CSV is fine — one prompt per row, include a short label column (e.g., \"factual\", \"multi-hop\", \"summary\").
2) Edge-case examples: flag ~20 queries that previously triggered incorrect answers or redaction concerns. Mark any that contain PII or HIPAA-like identifiers.
3) Data access note: do NOT include raw customer emails with full addresses; if you must, mask with <EMAIL_REDACTED> or replace domain names. We can provide a redaction checklist if helpful.
4) Benchmarks: if you have any existing internal evaluation metrics (accuracy, acceptable FPR for hallucinations), share as a PDF or spreadsheet.

Next steps from Redwood: 
- We will run a three-model sweep (one LLM family tuned for precision, one general medium-latency model, and a cost-optimized quantized variant) against your sample set and share a short deck with per-model token cost and p95 latency.
- Provide a short template for how you want outputs scored (0–3) so we align on quality thresholds.

Please upload the CSV to the Drive link below or attach to a reply. If it's easier, Monica can pick this up from a shared S3 bucket.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cSearchGridPromptSamples

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if there's any nuance on what to share.

Best,
Diego Fernandez

Thanks Diego — great summary and appreciated the clear asks. We're aligned on the buckets. Quick answers: 

- We'll export a 250-row CSV (covers the three buckets + a label column) and highlight 22 edge cases that tripped our prior evaluation.
- We'll run a light redaction pass before sharing. For anything that touches PII we'll replace with <REDACTED> and include an \"original_masking_notes\" column so you can see what was removed.
- Attached is a short PDF with our internal benchmark snapshots (latency & rough accuracy) — it's rough but should help you calibrate compute.

One question on your suggested model sweep: do you have a recommended starting family for short-answer precision vs. synthesis? We care about conservatism on legal language (prefer false negatives over hallucinated confident assertions).

Evan (cc'd) from engineering can chime in on how we can securely share the CSV (S3 presigned or Drive).

Thanks — we'll upload the CSV to the Drive link you provided and ping when it's live.

—Olivia

On Fri, Sep 18, 2026 at 4:18 PM Olivia Tran <olivia.tran@searchgrid.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Diego — great summary and appreciated the clear asks. We're aligned on the buckets...

Perfect — appreciate the rapid turnaround. A few quick clarifications and our recommended starter models: 

1) Redaction guidance (we'll send a short checklist): prefer token-level masking of emails/SSNs and replacing with consistent tokens (e.g., <EMAIL_REDACTED>, <SSN_REDACTED>) rather than free-text paraphrases. That preserves prompt shape for evaluation.

2) Scoring template: please include your internal \"acceptability\" column (0 = fail, 1 = minor issue, 2 = acceptable, 3 = excellent). We'll map that to our regression alerts.

3) Model recommendations (starter sweep):
- Precision-first: \"rw-precise-13b\" (higher context understanding, tuned for conservative answers)
- Balanced latency/cost: \"rw-balanced-7b-q4\" (good p95 latency on T4-like instances)
- Cost-optimized: \"meta-llama-2-13b-quant\" (aggressive quantization, watch for edge-case hallucinations)

We'll run these across your CSV and return: per-prompt output, a short confusion matrix for factual vs. hallucination flags, per-model p95 latency (on our standard infra), and token cost estimates. If any prompt triggers PII, we'll mark it and filter it from public artifacts; final deck will have redacted examples.

Ben and Monica — can you own the internal evaluation run and deliverables? Monica: please prepare the scoring sheet and attach a short README on how we define hallucination in this context. Ben: please map estimated monthly token spend for the balanced sweep vs. a production slicing plan.

Olivia — once you upload, we'll commit to a 5-working-day turnaround for the sweep and a one-hour results review with your team.

Thanks all — speak soon.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Office: +1 (415) 555-0148
